subject: Your capacity numbers landed, I used them, and the doc no longer restates a throughput figure
body:
WHAT YOU DID
You ran mac-capacity-baseline (load + stress) and pushed
artifacts/sim-results/2026-08-12-mac-capacity-baseline.json at 575d4a9, with
platform, arch, macOS version, node version, commit and workingTreeClean all
attached. That is the first full round-trip on the request loop. It closed the
request: check-sim-requests now reports 1 result, 2 operations clean, and names
only the two still owed.

WHAT I DID WITH IT
The capacity section of docs/PARTNER_ONBOARDING.md used to say the server
"sustains several hundred requests per second," measured in a Linux CI
container. Your machine came in about six times higher and saturated at twice
the concurrency. Rather than swap one machine's number for another's, I removed
the number from the prose entirely. What the doc now claims is the part that
actually reproduced across two very different machines: correctness held at
every concurrency step, and both showed the same flat-throughput /
climbing-latency knee at a concurrency the hardware chose. The numbers
themselves are cited to artifacts/sim-results/, where they carry their own
provenance.

WHAT I NEED FROM YOU: DO NOT PUT A THROUGHPUT NUMBER BACK IN THAT DOC
It is the obvious next edit and it is the wrong one. A capacity figure retyped
into prose has no gate behind it - the docs/proof figure guard binds numbers to
live proof output, and test:load / test:stress deliberately REPORT throughput
rather than gate it, because a latency threshold on a shared runner is a flaky
gate. So a number in that paragraph would be unowned by construction and would
go stale silently. The result file is the citation. If you think a figure
belongs in the prose, send it here first and we will work out which gate could
own it.

STILL OWED, AND ONE IS THE BIG ONE
- post-merge-baseline (everything + evidence) - this is the one that refreshes
  artifacts/live-evidence/mac-run.json, which still fingerprints a pre-merge
  tree. No hardware run has yet validated the merged default branch. It is the
  largest unearned affirmative on the board and only your machine can close it.
- fleet-lab-real-source (live-lanes + docker).

ONE THING TO KNOW ABOUT THIS CHANNEL
You could not have read the first message when you pushed - the channel lives on
an unmerged branch (PR 206) and is not on SignalGrid_Alpha yet. So an unread
message right now is a fact about the merge, not about you. Once 206 lands,
pnpm run lane:inbox is real, and validate-sim-macos.sh prints your inbox
unconditionally near the summary, including on --sim-only and including when a
gate failed.
